inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP_SWNO(58,57) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8. S11.VBS names this address swURFlip; its vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp write it from a staged right-flipper key only while vpmFlips.FlipperSolNumber(3) is non-zero, which core.vbs makes the default (sURFlipper = 34) unless the table calls NoUpperRightFlipper, directly or through core.vbs's cvpmFlips2.Init, which vpmInit runs and which calls it when the table defines cSingleRFlip as a number other than True. The constant does not follow the PinMAME column, and the ROM cannot read the address on this machine, so any such write has no effect.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP_SWNO(58,57) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 57 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 57: a host write to 57 is overwritten on the next update. The retained known-working script drives it: Diner_KeyDown and Diner_KeyUp pass the right flipper key to S11.VBS vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp (script lines 895 and 902), which set Controller.Switch(swLRFlip) with swLRFlip = 82 (excerpt vpm-script-library-flippers). In the Switch Levels run holding this address showed "RIGHT FLIPPER". The physical counterpart is the right cabinet flipper button (SW-10A-48), which fires the flipper coil through the flipper circuit and is sensed by its lane-change optotransistor on the Backbox Interconnect Board.

The driver declares FLIP_SWNO(58,57) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 58 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 47/48 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 58: a host write to 58 is overwritten on the next update. The retained known-working script drives it: Diner_KeyDown and Diner_KeyUp pass the left flipper key to S11.VBS vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp (script lines 895 and 902), which set Controller.Switch(swLLFlip) with swLLFlip = 84 (excerpt vpm-script-library-flippers). In the Switch Levels run holding this address showed "LEFT FLIPPER". The physical counterpart is the left cabinet flipper button (SW-10A-48), which fires the flipper coil through the flipper circuit and is sensed by its lane-change optotransistor on the Backbox Interconnect Board.

inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Upper Right End-of-Stroke (85)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWURFLIPEOSBIT = 0x10, published at 85 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP_SWNO(58,57) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8.

System 11's single Country jumper, read via core_getDip(0)<<7 on PIA2 PA7 (pinned s11.c labels it "Jumper W7"). The manual's ROM and Jumper Table lists the CPU board's installed jumpers (W1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 11, 14, 16, 17, and 19) and its Special Preset Adjustments (Install German 1-6 and others) are the operator-facing counterpart of a country setup.

mechanisms.behavior: A drained ball rests on the outhole switch (9) at the left end of the trough, and the Outhole Kicker (1, B-8039-2) kicks it into the trough, where up to three balls queue on Ball Trough #3 (13, left), #2 (12) and #1 (11, right, nearest the shooter lane; the ROM calls 11-13 TROUGH 1-3 BALL(S)). The Shooter Lane Feeder (22, Special #6, the C-9638 assembly) kicks the lead ball into the shooter lane (14). Three balls are installed but at most two are in play (2-ball Multi-Ball); the manual's Pinball Missing message reports a lost ball and the game runs on two. In the gameplay run the ROM fed the first ball at Start and repeated the feed 2 s later until trough #1 opened, and after the drain it kicked the outhole once. With no ball in the trough at power-up the ROM runs a ball search through 4, 1, 2, 5, 8 and 6. The retained script models the trough as one three-ball cvpmTrough.
mechanisms.label: Outhole and three-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: The left ramp's end is lifted and lowered by the B-11304-2 Ramp Elevator ("Ramp Mover"): Ramp Up (4, an AE-23-800 coil on the B-13655 bracket driving the A-11137 lift crank through a plunger) raises it and Ramp Down (2, the SM-1-26-600 coil working the A-11139 armature and lift-crank lock) releases it to drop; the assembly's microswitch (10, 5647-12001-00) reports the ramp's position. Shots up the left (Cash Register) ramp pass Left Ramp Exit (36) and advance the cash register value (lamps 1-5, adjustment 42). Spelling D-I-N-E-R raises the ramp so that a ball can be locked (lamp 12 LOCK; adjustments 34 and 43), and a locked ball leads to 2-ball Multi-Ball; the retained script calls the Lower Left Eject (50, kicked by 8) its "lock ramp saucer". In the gameplay run the ROM pulsed Ramp Down at Start and five more times about 0.8 s apart while 10 stayed open; the retained script closes 10 when its ramp is down and opens it when the ramp is up.
mechanisms.label: Cash Register (left) elevator ramp and lock

mechanisms.behavior: Two saucers on the left (B-9361-R-1 Eject Hole Arm assemblies): the Upper Left Eject (49, kicked by 5) at the top left, whose awards (adjustment 46) can also be reached from the sub-playfield shooter, and the Lower Left Eject (50, kicked by 8) under the Cash Register ramp, which holds the locked ball. In the gameplay run the ROM kicked each three times about 1.5 s apart while its switch stayed closed.
mechanisms.label: Upper and lower left eject holes

mechanisms.behavior: The right plastic ramp (D-13663) carries Right Ramp Entry (27) and Right Ramp Exit (28) micro switches. The Ramp Diverter (14, B-13346, coil AE-26-1500 per Amendment #1) on the ramp, when energized, sends the ball into the Coffee Cup (D-13660) at the top of the playfield: the ball passes Cup Entry (29) on the ramp and closes the Cup switch (17) in the cup. Spelling D-I-N-E-R "opens" the cup for the Cup Bonus (adjustment 43); the Cup Flashers (30) light it. In the gameplay run the ROM energized 14 as the ball passed 28 and released it when 17 closed 3.75 s later. The retained script swings its diverter primitive and drops a blocking wall while 14 is on.
mechanisms.label: Right ramp, diverter and coffee cup

mechanisms.behavior: A shot into Today's Special drops the ball below the playfield into the B-13652 Sub-Playfield Shooter, a bell-armature kicker (AE-23-800, solenoid 6) with a three-position switch bracket carrying Sub-Playfield Shooter 1 (15) and 2 (16), which count the balls waiting there. The shooter fires the ball up the 12-6904 wireform ("Sub-p'fld Shooter Ramp"), from which it can reach the Upper Left Eject (adjustment 46). Today's Special awards a random feature (adjustment 39), and with adjustment 34 it can start Multi-Ball while a ball is locked. With 15 held from power-up the ROM fired 6 repeatedly; in play it fired once about 6.9 s after 15 closed.
mechanisms.label: Today's Special sub-playfield shooter

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets (C-11223-1) in the centre: Hot Dog (22), Burger (23) and Chili (24), sensed by the optos of a C-13205 board and reset together by the AE-26-1200 coil (3). Lamps 30-32 sit in front of them. Completing a bank serves a customer (lamps 33-37, adjustment 37). In the gameplay run the ROM reset the bank at Start and, once all three were held down, retried the reset about every 0.6 s.
mechanisms.label: Center 3-bank drop targets (Hot Dog, Burger, Chili)

mechanisms.behavior: Three drop targets (C-11223-1) on the left: Root Beer (30, lower), Fries (31) and Iced Tea (32, upper), sensed by the optos of a second C-13205 board and reset together by the AE-26-1200 coil (13). Lamps 38-40 sit in front of them. In the gameplay run the ROM reset the bank at Start and, once all three were held down, retried about every 0.5 s.
mechanisms.label: Left 3-bank drop targets (Root Beer, Fries, Iced Tea)

mechanisms.behavior: The backbox clock (C-12036-3) turns one hand (decal 31-1559-571-2) on a wheel (03-8161) round a twelve-hour dial lit by lamps 49-60 (one per hour) and the Clock Flashers (31). A 14-7948 stepper motor (Motor & Connector Assy B-12088) is driven through the D-12045 Motor Control Board from Clock Wheel (A) (16) and (B) (15), and the board's opto (59) marks the home position. The manual's Wheel Test moves the hand to 12 o'clock (position 001), steps it clockwise to 11:59 (191), runs a "pendulum" sweep 001-191, 021-181 ... down to 111, and in Manual-Down mode lets the flipper buttons step it one position (a tenth of a step) either way. The ROM's Single Lamps test names 49-60 "WHEEL n O'CLOCK". At power-up the ROM drives 15 and 16 for about 7.7 s with the opto held either way, and in the Wheel Test the display counts the positions while 15 and 16 run; PinMAME's smoothed solenoid state does not resolve the individual steps. The retained script models a 60-step stepper cvpmMech on 15 and 16 with the opto at position 0 (vpmMechStepSol + vpmMechCircle), which is what a recreation needs to answer the ROM.
mechanisms.label: Backbox DINE-TIME clock

mechanisms.behavior: Three B-9414-1 jet bumpers with B-9415-1 coils in the upper centre: Left (17, switch 51), Right (19, switch 52) and Lower (21, switch 53). They are special solenoids, but dinerGameData maps no switch to them in PinMAME: the ROM fires each through its PIA line within one poll of its switch closing (gameplay run), so a consumer drives only the switch. The #44 bulbs in the caps are playfield G.I.
mechanisms.label: Three jet bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Two B-12665 slingshot kickers above the flippers (AE-26-1200 coils): Left (18) with its scoring switch 55 ("BL Kicker") and Right (20) with 54 ("BR Kicker"). Each also has a paired kicker actuating switch (A-4834-H + B-8734-1) that the Switches list prints without a matrix address. In PinMAME the ROM fires each special solenoid within one poll of its scoring switch closing (gameplay run).
mechanisms.label: Left and right slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: Two flippers (C-13174-R and -L, FL-11630/50VDC coils). The cabinet buttons (SW-10A-48) fire the coils through the flipper circuit, so no Sol. No. or driver is printed for them and PinMAME fabricates 45-48 from the buttons at public 82 and 84. A Flipper Lane Change optotransistor on the Backbox Interconnect Board senses each button for the CPU (58 left, 57 right), which core_updateSw copies from 84 and 82; the end-of-stroke switches in the coil circuit have no matrix address.
mechanisms.label: Two flippers, cabinet-wired

mechanisms.behavior: Three top rollover lanes E (19), A (20) and T (21) light the E-A-T lamps 22-24, each of which also lights the matching letter of the raised sign at the back of the playfield; the Grill Bonus standup (18, B-12912-4) advances the Grill Bonus ladder (lamps 41-45); the spinner (56) is lit by lamp 16.
mechanisms.label: E-A-T top lanes, Grill Bonus standup and spinner

mechanisms.behavior: Static toys lit by the lamp matrix: the Cash Register (B-13656) at the left shows the 20K-100K values (lamps 1-5), and the Jukebox (C-13661) at the top right shows lamps 25-29. The left and right DINER People assemblies (B-13764-1 and -2: Haji, Babs, Cook and Boris, Buck, Pepe decals on wood spacers), printed on the clock's page, carry no lamp, coil or switch.
mechanisms.label: Cash register, jukebox and backbox people

mechanisms.behavior: The A/C Select Relay (12) on the Aux Power Driver Board switches the solenoid supply between the "A" and "C" terminals so that each of the eight switched drivers (Q22-Q25, Q30-Q33) serves an "A" coil while it is released and a "C" flasher while it is energized. Pinned PinMAME publishes the C loads separately at 25-32 and copies the relay's state into switch 2, the relay's C-side contact the ROM checks in its C-Side test.
mechanisms.label: A/C solenoid select relay

mechanisms.behavior: The A-side load of pair 07 (7, AE-23-800) raps the B-10686-1 Knocker Assembly in the backbox for replays and specials.
mechanisms.label: Backbox knocker

physical.notes: Solenoid Table entry 01A ("Outhole Kicker"). Switched pair 01A/01C on driver Q33: the "A" load is pulsed with the A/C Select Relay (12) de-energized and the "C" load with it energized (the table's note 3). Pinned updsol publishes the A load at 1 and the C load at 25. The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 1 of 30 while the upper display shows "OUTHOLE". In the gameplay run the ROM fired it once the drained ball closed the outhole switch (9); with 9 held from power-up it retried 11 times in 14 s (power-up probe). Retained script: bsTrough.SolIn (line 339), which kicks a drained ball from the Outhole kicker into the trough. Placed at the retained table's Kicker Outhole, a documented projection onto the drain kicker the script's cvpmTrough receives balls on; the outhole kicker coil has no object of its own.

Solenoid Table entry 02A ("Ramp Down"). Switched pair 02A/02C on driver Q25: the "A" load is pulsed with the A/C Select Relay (12) de-energized and the "C" load with it energized (the table's note 3). Pinned updsol publishes the A load at 2 and the C load at 26. The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 3 of 30 while the upper display shows "RAMP DOWN". In the gameplay run the ROM pulsed it at Start and five more times about 0.8 s apart while the Up/Down switch (10) stayed open, then stopped. Retained script: SolRampDown (line 362), which lowers the table's lock ramp and closes switch 10 when it is down (lines 662-686). Placed at the retained table's Primitive lockramp (object position), a documented projection onto the lock ramp, the moving part the B-11304-2 Ramp Elevator's SM-1-26-600 armature coil lowers.

Solenoid Table entry 03A ("Center 3-Bk Dr Tgt Reset"); the Solenoids/Flashers list prints "Cen 3-Bk Dr Tgt Reset". Switched pair 03A/03C on driver Q32: the "A" load is pulsed with the A/C Select Relay (12) de-energized and the "C" load with it energized (the table's note 3). Pinned updsol publishes the A load at 3 and the C load at 27. The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 5 of 30 while the upper display shows "CENTER DROP BANK". In the gameplay run the ROM pulsed it at Start and, once all three centre targets (22-24) were held down, four times 0.6 s apart. Retained script: dtright.SolDropUp (line 359), raising the centre drop targets 22-24. Placed at the retained table's HitTarget burger, the bank's middle target, a documented projection onto the bank's middle drop target; the reset coil sits below the bank and has no object of its own.

Solenoid Table entry 04A ("Ramp Up"). Switched pair 04A/04C on driver Q24: the "A" load is pulsed with the A/C Select Relay (12) de-energized and the "C" load with it energized (the table's note 3). Pinned updsol publishes the A load at 4 and the C load at 28. The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 7 of 30 while the upper display shows "RAMP UP". At power-up, with no ball in the trough, the ROM pulses it twice in its ball search (power-up probes). Retained script: SolRampUp (line 361), which raises the lock ramp and opens switch 10 when it is up (lines 670-686). Placed at the retained table's Primitive lockramp (object position), a documented projection onto the lock ramp, which the B-11304-2 Ramp Elevator's AE-23-800 coil and lift crank raise.

Solenoid Table entry 05A ("Upper Left Eject"). Switched pair 05A/05C on driver Q31: the "A" load is pulsed with the A/C Select Relay (12) de-energized and the "C" load with it energized (the table's note 3). Pinned updsol publishes the A load at 5 and the C load at 29. The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 9 of 30 while the upper display shows "UPPER LEFT EJECT". In the gameplay run the ROM pulsed it three times about 1.5 s apart while switch 49 was held closed; with 49 and 50 held from power-up it retried 7 times (power-up probe). Retained script: SolUpperEject (line 346), bsUpperEject.SolOut on Kicker UpperEject. Placed at the retained table's Kicker UpperEject. The factory drawing (Diner manual PDF 77, printed DINER 73) ends callout 5A's leader 0.076 normalized from it, beyond the 0.07 limit, so this placement stays observed.

Solenoid Table entry 06A ("Sub-P'fld Shooter"); the Solenoids/Flashers list prints "Sub-Playfield Shooter". Switched pair 06A/06C on driver Q23: the "A" load is pulsed with the A/C Select Relay (12) de-energized and the "C" load with it energized (the table's note 3). Pinned updsol publishes the A load at 6 and the C load at 30. The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 11 of 30 while the upper display shows "SUB-PFLD SHOOTER". With 15 (or 15 and 16) held from power-up the ROM pulsed it 7-8 times in 12 s (power-up probes); in the gameplay run it fired once, about 6.9 s after 15 closed. Retained script: SolSubPlfdShooter (line 349), which fires bsSubWay out of Kicker SubWaypopper when it holds a ball. Placed at the retained table's Kicker SubWaypopper, a documented projection onto the popper the script fires the sub-playfield ball from; the B-13652 shooter coil has no object of its own.

Solenoid Table entry 07A ("Knocker (in Backbox)"); the Solenoids/Flashers list prints "Knocker (Backbox)". Switched pair 07A/07C on driver Q30: the "A" load is pulsed with the A/C Select Relay (12) de-energized and the "C" load with it energized (the table's note 3). Pinned updsol publishes the A load at 7 and the C load at 31. The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 13 of 30 while the upper display shows "KNOCKER". Retained script: vpmSolSound Knocker (lines 341 and 358). The manual puts it in the backbox ("Knocker (in Backbox)"; Knocker Assembly B-10686-1).

Solenoid Table entry 08A ("Lower Left Eject"). Switched pair 08A/08C on driver Q22: the "A" load is pulsed with the A/C Select Relay (12) de-energized and the "C" load with it energized (the table's note 3). Pinned updsol publishes the A load at 8 and the C load at 32. The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 15 of 30 while the upper display shows "LOWER LEFT EJECT". In the gameplay run the ROM pulsed it three times about 1.5 s apart while switch 50 was held closed. Retained script: SolLowKicker (line 345), bsLowKicker.SolOut on Kicker Lowkicker. Placed at the retained table's Kicker Lowkicker.

Solenoid Table entry 09 ("Right Ramp Flashers"); the Solenoids/Flashers list prints "Right Ramp Flash". Solenoid Type "Controlled". The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 17 of 30 while the upper display shows "RT. RAMP FLASHERS". Retained script: SolFlash9 (line 347), lighting the two right flasher domes Flasher1 and Flasher2. The Solenoid Table prints 2p,1g: two playfield bulbs and one backglass bulb. The playfield bulbs are the two right flasher domes the script lights for this address (Flasher1 at the right ramp's top and Flasher2 further down it), which are the placements; the backglass bulb has no playfield position.

Solenoid Table entry 10 ("Backbox/Pl'fld  Illum Relay"); the Solenoids/Flashers list prints "B'box/P'fld G I Relays*". Solenoid Type "Controlled". The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 18 of 30 while the upper display shows "GEN. ILLUMINATION". In the gameplay run the ROM energized it from the third plumb-bob tilt until the next ball started, the only span it was held in play. Retained script: SolGIRelay (line 356), which turns every Light of its lightsGI collection off while the solenoid is on. This output drives two relays (5580-09555-01, K1 on each of two C-11998-1 General Illumination Relay Boards, the table's note 4a), one under the playfield and one on the backbox insert board, which switch the playfield and the backbox general illumination (the Solenoids/Flashers list prints "B'box/P'fld G I Relays" with the footnote "for both Playfield and Backbox General Illumination"). The Locations Diagram lists the relay board under both and labels the insert-board one "Rly Bd Sol. 10" while its parts list prints "Relay Board (Sol. 11 Gen. Illum)"; the Solenoid Table, the Solenoids/Flashers list and the ROM's "GEN. ILLUMINATION" all put it at 10. Energized means G.I. off: the ROM holds it through a tilt, the retained script turns its lightsGI collection off while it is on, and pinned PinMAME types it as a reverse-acting #44 "Playfield GI output". The manual prints no G.I. bulb count or layout; the placements are the 28 bulb lights of the retained table's lightsGI collection (each GIn Light and the bulb-mesh light in each jet bumper cap). A table's G.I. grouping is not the machine's wiring, so these placements stay observed and no quantity is asserted.

Solenoid Table entry 11 ("Left Ramp Flashers"); the Solenoids/Flashers list prints "Left Ramp Flash". Solenoid Type "Controlled". The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 19 of 30 while the upper display shows "LT. RAMP FLASHERS". Retained script: SolFlash11 (line 348), lighting the two left flasher domes Flasher3 and Flasher4. The Solenoid Table prints 2p, both on the playfield. They are the two left flasher domes the script lights for this address (Flasher3 beside the upper left loop and Flasher4 in the top left corner), which are the placements; the solenoid drawing marks callout 11 twice at the same two places.

Solenoid Table entry 12 ("A/C Select Relay"); the Solenoids/Flashers list prints "A/C Select Relay**". Solenoid Type "Controlled". The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 20 of 30 while the upper display shows "A/C SELECT". The ROM energizes it ahead of every C-side step of the Coil Test and releases it for every A-side step, and alternates it about every 2 s in the C-Side test. Retained script: SolACSelect (line 357), a relay sound only. The A/C select relay (5580-09555-01, note 5: "mounted on Aux Power Driver Bd, D-12247, in the backbox"). Pinned PinMAME publishes its own state here and, while it is pulsed, moves the low solenoid byte to 25-32; it also copies this state into switch 2 (S11_MUXSW2), the relay's C-side contact the ROM reads.

Solenoid Table entry 13 ("Left 3-Bk Dr Tgt Reset"). Solenoid Type "Controlled". The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 21 of 30 while the upper display shows "LEFT DROP BANK". In the gameplay run the ROM pulsed it at Start and, once all three left targets (30-32) were held down, four times 0.5 s apart. Retained script: dtleft.SolDropUp (line 360), raising the left drop targets 30-32. Placed at the retained table's HitTarget fries, the bank's middle target, a documented projection onto the bank's middle drop target; the reset coil sits below the bank and has no object of its own.

Solenoid Table entry 14 ("Diverter"). Solenoid Type "Controlled". The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 22 of 30 while the upper display shows "DIVERTER". In the gameplay run the ROM energized it as the ball passed Right Ramp Exit (28) and held it 3.75 s, until the ball closed the Cup switch (17). Retained script: Sol14Diverter (line 363), which swings the right-ramp diverter divider179to201 and drops its blocking wall Sol14Closed. Amendment #1 corrects the Solenoid Table's AE-26-1200 to AE-26-1500 for this coil (and item 6 of the B-13346 Ramp Diverter Assembly), so the part number follows the amendment. The diverter sits on the right ramp: energized, it turns right-ramp shots into the cup (adjustment 43 "DINER RAMP" sets how easily it "opens" the cup). Placed at the retained table's Primitive divider179to201 (pivot, object position), a documented projection onto the diverter's pivot; the B-13346 Ramp Diverter coil sits under the right ramp and has no object of its own.

Solenoid Table entry 15 ("Clock Wheel (B)"); the Solenoids/Flashers list prints "Clock Wheel Motor (B)". Solenoid Type "Controlled". The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 23 of 30 while the upper display shows "WHEEL B". At power-up the ROM drives 15 and 16 for about 7.7 s whether the clock opto (59) is held open or closed (power-up probes), and the Wheel Test steps them continuously; PinMAME's smoothed solenoid state shows the stepper's phases as long on-spans, not as individual steps. Retained script: the cvpmMech WheelMech (.Sol1 = 15, line 455), a stepper-solenoid mechanism driving the backglass clock hand. One of the two windings (phases A and B) of the 14-7948 stepper motor of the backbox DINE-TIME clock (C-12036-3, Motor & Connector Assy B-12088 on the D-12045 Motor Control Board); the drive connections 2J4-15/16 and 2J11 stay in the backbox. The clock's single hand steps round the dial, homing on the Clock Wheel opto (59); see the clock mechanism.

Solenoid Table entry 16 ("Clock Wheel (A)"); the Solenoids/Flashers list prints "Clock Wheel Motor (A)". Solenoid Type "Controlled". The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 24 of 30 while the upper display shows "WHEEL A". See solenoid 15. Retained script: the cvpmMech WheelMech (.Sol2 = 16, line 455). One of the two windings (phases A and B) of the 14-7948 stepper motor of the backbox DINE-TIME clock (C-12036-3, Motor & Connector Assy B-12088 on the D-12045 Motor Control Board); the drive connections 2J4-15/16 and 2J11 stay in the backbox. The clock's single hand steps round the dial, homing on the Clock Wheel opto (59); see the clock mechanism.

Solenoid Table entry 17 ("Left Jet Bumper"). Solenoid Type "Special #1". The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 25 of 30 while the upper display shows "LEFT JET". dinerGameData is a plain INITGAME with no sxx.ssSw entries, so PinMAME publishes this special solenoid only when the ROM drives its PIA line itself (setSSSol, WMS ssSolNo order); the Coil Test shows the printed Special numbers 1-6 at public 17-22. In the gameplay run the ROM fired it within one poll of switch 51 closing. Retained script: vpmSolSound bumperleft (line 342). Placed at the retained table's Bumper LeftJetBumper.
